arxiv-1604-03494.title: Tuning quantum measurements to control chaos
arxiv-1604-03494.creator: Jessica K. Eastman, Joseph J. Hope, André R. R. Carvalho
arxiv-1604-03494.description: Abstract Environment-induced decoherence has long been recognised as being of crucial importance in the study of chaos in quantum systems. In particular, the exact form and strength of the system-environment interaction play a major role in the quantum-to-classical transition of chaotic systems. arxiv-2110-07503.title: Revisiting timelike geodesics in the Fisher/Janis–Newman–Winicour–Wyman spacetime
arxiv-2110-07503.creator: Keisuke Ota, Shinpei Kobayashi, Keisuke Nakashi
arxiv-2110-07503.description: Abstract We investigate the timelike geodesics and the periapsis precession of orbits in the Fisher-Janis-Newman-Winicour-Wyman spacetime. This spacetime represents the naked singularity spacetime in the Einstein-massless scalar system. We revisit the results in the previous studies and relax the assumptions about the eccentricity of a bound orbit and the size of a semilatus.

arxiv-2202-08548.title: From Utility to Capability: A New Paradigm to Conceptualize and Develop Inclusive PETs Conference: FULL CONF NAME; DATE; LOCATION Price: 15.00
arxiv-2202-08548.creator: Partha Das Chowdhury, Andrés Domínguez Hernández, Kopo M. Ramokapane, Awais Rashid
arxiv-2202-08548.description: Abstract . The wider adoption of PETs ( PETs ) has relied on usability studies – which focus mainly on an assessment of how a specified group of users interface, in particular contexts, with the technical properties of a system.

arxiv-2206-05217.title: Bulge formation inside quiescent lopsided stellar disks: connecting accretion, star formation and morphological transformation in a z ∼ 3 \rm z\sim 3 galaxy group Preprint: Boris S. Kalita
arxiv-2206-05217.creator: Boris S. Kalita, Emanuele Daddi, Frederic Bournaud, R. Michael Rich, Francesco Valentino, Carlos Gómez-Guijarro, Sandrine Codis, Ivan Delvecchio, David Elbaz, Veronica Strazzullo, Victor de Sousa Magalhaes, Jérôme Pety, Qinghua Tan
arxiv-2206-05217.description: Abstract We present well-resolved near-IR and sub-mm analysis of the three highly star-forming massive ( > 10 11 ​ M ⊙ >10^{11}\,\rm M_{\odot} ) galaxies within the core of the RO-1001 galaxy group at z = 2.91 \rm z=2.91 .

arxiv-2302-01304.title: Observations of peak electric load growth in ERCOT with the rise of electrified heating and its implications for future resource planning Journal: Journal of L a T e X Templates
arxiv-2302-01304.creator: Matthew J. Skiles, Joshua D. Rhodes, PhD, Michael E. Webber, PhD
arxiv-2302-01304.description: Abstract This analysis quantitatively compares the evolution in summer and winter peak demands in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) service area from 1997 through 2021. Weather data for the days in which peak demand occurred were also compiled to investigate the relationship between peak heating and cooling loads and ambient temperature.

arxiv-2406-09615.title: Strain rate controls alignment in growing bacterial monolayers
arxiv-2406-09615.creator: Blake Langeslay 1, Gabriel Juarez 2
arxiv-2406-09615.description: Abstract Growing monolayers of rod-shaped bacteria exhibit local alignment similarly to extensile active nematics. When confined in a channel or growing inward from a ring, the local nematic order of these monolayers changes to a global ordering with cells throughout the monolayer orienting in the same direction.

pmc-10640573.title: Characteristics of lactate metabolism phenotype in hepatocellular carcinoma
pmc-10640573.creator: Jiacheng Zhang, Keshuai Dong, Xin Zhang, Chunlei Li, Jia Yu, Weixing Wang
pmc-10640573.description: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a highly heterogeneous cancer, and more effective prognostic markers are needed. Lactic acid has been proved to be an important metabolite involved in cancer development, metastasis, and the tumor microenvironment, affecting the prognosis of patients. The role of lactic acid metabolism regulators (LAMRs) in HCC is still unclear.

pmc-11431246.title: Effects of Dietary Supplementation with Cocrystals of Thymol and Carvacrol on Quality, Nutrient Composition, and Oxidative Stability of Broiler Meat
pmc-11431246.creator: Yang Li, Changjin Li, Yunlong Zhang, Nadia Everaert, Luke Comer, Libo Huang, Ning Jiao, Xuejun Yuan, Weiren Yang, Shuzhen Jiang, Piotr Domaradzki, Mariusz Florek
pmc-11431246.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Consumer demand for high-quality meat has increased. This study aimed to investigate the potential application of cocrystals of thymol and carvacrol in broilers for high-quality meat production. Eight hundred 1-day-old chicks were assigned to four groups fed diets supplemented with 0, 40, 60, and 80 mg/kg of Crystal EO® (CEO), containing 25% cocrystals of thymol and carvacrol in a 42-d feeding trial.

pmc-11440299.title: Ultrasound effect on a biorefinery lignin-cellulose mixture
pmc-11440299.creator: Kait Kaarel Puss, Peeter Paaver, Mart Loog, Siim Salmar
pmc-11440299.description: Forest biorefineries provide multiple new avenues for applied research. The main concept lies in the malleability of the processes and their stepwise organization. The core element of the biorefinery concept addressed in the present study is the pretreatment step; here, wood biomass is converted into free hemicellulosic sugars, lignin and cellulose.

pmc-11596215.title: Comparison of Bone Mineral Density Between Veterans and Non-Veterans and Its Impact on Fracture Risk Assessment
pmc-11596215.creator: Ya-Lien Deng, Chun-Sheng Hsu, Yi-Ming Chen, Shih-Yi Lin, Tse-Yu Chen, Chi-Ruei Li, Hsu-Tung Lee, Ying-Chia Wu, Mikk Jürisson
pmc-11596215.description: Background and Objectives: Osteoporosis poses significant health risks, especially among veterans, due to lifestyle factors. This study compares bone density and fracture risks between male veterans and non-veterans. Materials and Methods: We conducted a retrospective analysis of 1427 veterans from the Taichung Veterans General Hospital osteoporosis database (2010–2022), matched 1:1 by age and gender with non-veterans.

pmc-11616571.title: Ultrasonic depolymerization of pomegranate peel pectin: Effect of sonication time on antioxidant, α-amylase inhibitory, and prebiotic properties
pmc-11616571.creator: Sahar Bachari, Maryam Ghaderi-Ghahfarokhi, Hassan Ahmadi Gavlighi, Mehdi Zarei
pmc-11616571.description: This study aimed to investigate the effects of ultrasonic treatment time (5–30 min) on the structural characteristics, antioxidant, α-amylase inhibitory, and prebiotic properties of pomegranate peel pectin (PPP). The extracted PPP was rich in galacturonic acid (64.27 %) and exhibited a high degree of esterification (DE, 61.7 %), with an average molecular weight (Mw) of 135.6 kDa.

pmc-12944772.title: Second-dose measles vaccination coverage and associated factors among children aged 19 to 35 months in Debre Birhan city, Ethiopia, 2024: A community-based cross-sectional study
pmc-12944772.creator: Tebabere Moltot, Zenebe Abebe Gebreegziabher, Agmasie Damtew Walle, Mistire Nigussie, Micheal Amera Tizazu, Addisalem Workie Demsash, Eyosias Yeshialem, Edison Mworozi, Edison Mworozi, Tebelay Dilnessa, Tebelay Dilnessa, Tebelay Dilnessa
pmc-12944772.description: BackgroundAchieving high coverage of both measles vaccine doses is essential for herd immunity. Despite high first-dose coverage, measles outbreaks persist in Debre Birhan City, Ethiopia. Therefore, this study aimed to assess second-dose measles vaccine coverage.and its associated factors among children aged 19–35 months in Debre Birhan City, Ethiopia.

pmc-13063881.title: Effect of different dentin etching protocols on the immediate microtensile bond strength of two bulk-fill restorative systems in class I cavities
pmc-13063881.creator: Eman H Albelasy, Ahmed Gamal Raghip, Hoda Saleh Ismail
pmc-13063881.description: BackgroundReliable bonding to dentin in high C-factor cavities remains a clinical challenge due to polymerization stress. Bulk-fill composites, including self- and dual-cured systems, aim to simplify placement and improve adaptation in deep cavities. However, limited data exist on how different dentin surface treatments affect their bond strength.

pmc-13230740.title: autoFISH: a modular toolbox for sequential single-molecule RNA FISH experiments
pmc-13230740.creator: Christian Weber, Thomas Defard, Chloé Sturmach, Mickael Lelek, Hugo Laporte, Ayan Mallick, Maria Isabella Gariboldi, José-Arturo Londoño-Vallejo, Thomas Walter, Charles Fouillade, Jacques Bourg, Florian Mueller
pmc-13230740.description: Understanding the role of gene expression in cellular function and tissue organization requires spatial and quantitative detection of individual RNA molecules. Yet, the widespread adoption of automated single-molecule fluorescence in situ hybridization (smFISH) has been limited by the cost of equipment and the complexity of experimental procedures.

pmc-13519537.title: A Cerebral Organoid Model of Familial Alzheimer’s Disease Using Amyloid Precursor Protein Mutation, Val669Leu (APPSeoul)
pmc-13519537.creator: Won Hee Jung, Seung Tack Oh, Mu Seog Choe, Yu Jin Kwon, So Jin Kim, Ye Seong Jeon, Kyung Min Baek, Woochul Chang, Kyung Seob Lim, Joong Sun Kim, Seung Pil Yun, Min Young Lee

pmc-13546524.title: Evolving burden of pancreatic cancer in the Middle East and North Africa Region, 1990–2023: an analysis based on the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023
pmc-13546524.creator: Emad Aljohani, Abdullah Albarrak, Badr F Al-Khateeb, Noof Alwatban, Khadijah Angawi, Maryam Alhabas, Raed Aldahash, Amani Alharthy, Abdullah T Alanazi, Ashraf El-Metwally
pmc-13546524.description: BackgroundPancreatic cancer is a highly lethal malignancy characterized by an aggressive biological behavior and a narrow therapeutic window, making it a significant public health challenge. In the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, monitoring the evolving disease burden is essential for identifying high-risk populations and guiding the allocation of resources for early detection and palliative care.

uslaw-usc-t29-s2502.title: 29 U.S.C. § 2502 — Outreach to employers and labor unions
uslaw-usc-t29-s2502.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t29-s2502.description: United States Code, Title 29 (Labor); Chapter 27 (Women In Apprenticeship And Nontraditional Occupations). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In general With funds available to the Secretary of Labor to carry out the operations of the Department of Labor in fiscal year 1994 and subsequent fiscal years, the Secretary shall carry out an outreach program to inform employers of technical assistance.
